reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about the existence, structure, and temperature-dependent behavior of a natural oxide film on Q235 steel, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific corrosion behavior of this particular steel grade under the stated conditions.
premises: A naturally formed protective oxide layer exists on as-rolled Q235 steel
At room temperature, this oxide layer is compact and limits corrosive attack in chloride-rich environments
At elevated temperatures, the oxide film degrades (becomes porous/defective) and accelerates localized corrosion
Faster oxidation kinetics at elevated temperatures produce a less adherent, porous oxide film
